title: Variables
description: Learn how to store your treasures using magic boxes called Variables.

content.value: Imagine you have a bunch of magic boxes. You can put anything you want inside these boxes—like a number, a secret word, or even your favorite color. In Python, these magic boxes are called Variables!

Why do we need them? Well, computers have terrible memories! If you don't put things in a box with a label on it, the computer will forget them immediately. So, we create a box, stick a label on it (a name), and put our treasure (a value) inside.
To create a variable, you just write the label you want, an equals sign `=`, and then what you want to put inside. Like this:
Now, whenever you ask Python for `toys`, it will look inside the box labeled 'toys' and give you the number 10.
Always give your boxes good names! If you label a box `x`, you might forget what's inside. But if you label it `score`, you know exactly what it is.
To see what's inside your box, you can use our `print` spell from the last lesson! Just put the name of the box inside the print spell.

practice.question: Create a magic box named 'age', put your age inside it (like 10 or 12), and print it!
